guidelines.title: equivalent content both official languages
guidelines.rule: Equivalent content in both official languages — professionally translated; Canadian EN/FR conventions; bilingual images, multimedia and transcripts (or equivalent information in both languages). Not a “summary in the other language.” Dual-cite USWDS language selector (full equivalent translations) vs Canada Official-Language keep-place toggle — two jobs; this row is content equivalence, not the toggle control.

citation.source: Canada.ca — Designing content; Designing content for Canada.ca

pass_when: EN and FR are equivalent professional translations, including media/transcripts or equivalent information.
fail_when: Other language is only a summary, or media exists in one official language only with no equivalent.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Keep-place language toggle as this row; USWDS 2-vs-3+ selector as this row.

guidelines.title: four writing qualities
guidelines.rule: Four writing qualities: intuitive / comprehensive / targeted / consistent — just enough for a first-time user to finish alone; enough depth for specialists; most important first (don’t dump every option); standardized so people can scan with trust.

citation.source: Canada.ca — Designing content; Designing content for Canada.ca

pass_when: Copy lets a first-time user finish, keeps specialist depth, leads with the important, and stays consistent for scanning.
fail_when: Every option dumped up front; first-time user cannot finish alone; inconsistent patterns that block scanning.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Inverted pyramid (next row) as this qualities list.

guidelines.title: inverted pyramid no welcome filler
guidelines.rule: Inverted pyramid; no welcome-message filler. Most important idea/step first; then prioritized tasks; extra detail last and only if it supports the task. Stay on topic; no “welcome to our site” or background for its own sake.

citation.source: Canada.ca — Designing content; Content Style Guide

pass_when: Lead is the main idea/step; extra detail is last and task-supporting; no welcome/background filler.
fail_when: Welcome-to-our-site opener, or background before the task.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Four writing qualities as this structure row.

guidelines.title: you your never i my
guidelines.rule: You/your; never I/my; we = Government of Canada. Second person in titles, links, nav (“Replace your card”). Don’t switch to speaking as the user. “My” only in proper names (My Service Canada Account). Name a specific institution only when that institution will contact / be contacted, or its role matters to the task.
pass_when: Titles/links/nav use you/your; we is GC; “My” only in proper names; institutions named only when they matter to the task.
fail_when: I/my in UI chrome; speaking as the user; a specific institution named with no task reason.

guidelines.title: must need may might
guidelines.rule: must (law) vs need to (admin) vs may/might (permission) — not “legally required to.” Don’t use can/could for permission (those mean ability).
pass_when: Legal obligation = must; admin = need to; permission = may/might.
fail_when: “Legally required to”; can/could used for permission.

guidelines.title: no eg ie spell out and
guidelines.rule: No e.g. / i.e.; spell out “and.” Use “for example” / “that is.” Ampersand only in proper names and set abbreviations (R&D, O&M). Latin abbreviations only when space is tight (tables).
pass_when: Prose uses “for example” / “that is” and “and”; & only in proper names/set abbreviations.
fail_when: e.g. / i.e. in prose, or & used as “and” outside names/abbreviations.

guidelines.title: underline links only no italics emphasis
guidelines.rule: Underline = links only; no italics for emphasis — italics are hard for dyslexia; use bold sparingly. Don’t combine underline+bold except the topic-page hyperlink style.
pass_when: Underline is only for links; emphasis is not italics; underline+bold only on the named topic-page hyperlink style.
fail_when: Underlined non-links; italics used for emphasis; underline+bold on ordinary text.

guidelines.title: unique title one h1 heading every 200 words
guidelines.rule: Unique page title; one H1; a heading about every 200 words. Title makes sense alone, keywords first, no trailing punctuation, no boast copy. Publication/program titles are usually bad web titles. Heading 1 once.
pass_when: Unique title (keywords first, no trailing punctuation/boast); exactly one H1; headings break long copy (~every 200 words).
fail_when: Duplicate/boast title; multiple H1s; long unheaded slabs.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Doormat heading character caps as this row.

guidelines.title: lists max 7 or split
guidelines.rule: Lists ≤7 items, or split by category. One idea per bullet; consistent grammar; numbered only for rank/order/steps. Lead-in must apply to every item (“all of” vs “one or more”).
pass_when: A list is ≤7 or split by category; numbered only for rank/order/steps; lead-in applies to every item.
fail_when: 8+ undifferentiated items; numbered list with no order; lead-in that does not apply to every item.

guidelines.title: tables no blank cells
guidelines.rule: Tables: no blank cells; split complex tables. Every column/row has a header; cell value relates to both. If empty: notes/legend or “no data” / “0” / “n/a” — never a silent blank. Convert simple data to a list; never nested subheads inside a column.
pass_when: Headers on rows/columns; empty values are named (“no data” / “0” / “n/a” / legend); simple data is a list; no nested subheads in a column.
fail_when: Silent blank cells; missing headers; nested subheads in a column.
guidelines.do_not_claim: NSW chart data-table anatomy as this row.

guidelines.title: functional alt 140 decorative empty
guidelines.rule: Functional alt ≈140 characters; decorative `alt=""`; long description if more. Describe as if on the phone; don’t write “image of…”. If equivalent explanation already sits next to the figure, skip the long desc. Transcripts for pre-recorded audio/video (dialogue, on-screen text, important sound/action).
pass_when: Functional images have concise alt (about 140 characters, not “image of”); decorative `alt=""`; longer meaning has a long desc unless equivalent text is already beside the figure; pre-recorded AV has a transcript.
fail_when: Missing alt; “image of…” filler; decorative images with long alt; no transcript for pre-recorded AV that needs one.
guidelines.do_not_claim: WCAG SC numbers as this row.

guidelines.title: no click here same text same destination
guidelines.rule: No “click here” / “read more”; same text → same destination. Unique descriptive text per distinct URL; same words when two links go to the same page. Don’t bury the task-critical link mid-paragraph. Downloads: file type + size in parentheses inside the link. Other-language / duration likewise in parentheses inside the link.
pass_when: Link text describes the destination; identical text shares a destination; file type/size (and other-language/duration) sit inside the link; task-critical links are not buried mid-paragraph.
fail_when: “Click here” / “read more”; same text to different URLs; type/size only outside the link.

guidelines.title: intranet destinations labelled
guidelines.rule: Intranet destinations: “(accessible only on the Government of Canada network)” — public pages must not silently link behind the GC network. (Not a contact pattern.)
pass_when: Public-page links to GC-network-only destinations include that parenthetical.
fail_when: A public page silently links behind the GC network.

guidelines.title: find understand use nonpriority must not block
guidelines.rule: Find / understand / use; non-priority must not block findability. Every design decision is judged on those three. Group the same public topic across departments; remove duplicate content. Do not publish what GC is not the authoritative source for — link out instead.

citation.source: Canada.ca — Designing content; Designing content for Canada.ca

pass_when: Non-priority content does not hide the findable task; duplicate public topics are grouped/removed; non-authoritative material is a link out.
fail_when: Extra non-priority blocks findability; duplicate departmental pages for the same public topic; GC publishes what it is not the source for.

guidelines.title: no separate mobile site
guidelines.rule: No separate mobile site — same content on phone and desktop; IA as flat as possible; in-page navigation over menus; limit page weight. Dual-cite USWDS continuity / mobile-friendly without a second origin and Wayfinding Jump to Item (do not merge with USWDS tab-before-main / never-link-externally in-page row).
pass_when: Phone and desktop share the same content origin; IA is flat; in-page nav is preferred over extra menus.
fail_when: A separate mobile origin/site, or a second menu instead of in-page nav on a long page.
guidelines.do_not_claim: USWDS in-page tab-before-main geometry as this row.

guidelines.title: doormats max 9
guidelines.rule: Doormats: ≤9; heading 45 (max 75); description 120 keywords. Linked heading, no end punctuation. Descriptions = comma-separated keywords, not full sentences; no “Includes… / Information on… / Learn more about…”; no nested links, promo, bold, or bullets; no decorative icons. Don’t repeat Most-requested links. Semantic h2 “Services and information” may be visually hidden. Single-column when sequential tasks or heights would gap.
pass_when: ≤9 doormats; heading/description within those lengths; keyword descriptions; no nested links/promo/bold/bullets/decorative icons; no Most-requested repeats.
fail_when: 10+ doormats; sentence descriptions with “Learn more about…”; nested links or decorative icons; Most-requested duplicated.

guidelines.title: interactive questions max 7 same place
guidelines.rule: Interactive questions: ≤7; one at a time in the same place. Written to “you”; choices immediately under the question as answers; Continue/context-specific button (not “Next” if the page already has Next in multi-page nav); always a way back (“change your selection”). Dual-cite GOV.UK one-question-per-page (Canada keeps subsequent questions on the same page in the same slot). Pre-select most-common vs GOV.UK do-not-preselect is not a NEW row.
pass_when: ≤7 questions, one visible at a time in the same slot; you-voice; choices as answers under the question; Continue is not a conflicting “Next”; a way back exists.
fail_when: Many questions shown at once; “Next” clashes with page Next; no way to change a selection.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A winner vs GOV.UK one-question-per-page; a NEW pre-select rule.

guidelines.title: supertask once never promo
guidelines.rule: Supertask button once; never for promo; link-style button for rare actions. Supertask launches the page’s main task (apply / calculator / wizard). Not for promotion (use feature patterns). Primary still ≤1 per page (dual-cite Actions). Link buttons = infrequent (restart calculator) with a larger hit area than a text link. Danger only when consequences are real.
pass_when: At most one supertask; it starts the main task; not used for promo; ≤1 primary; link-style only for rare actions with a larger hit area; danger only for real consequences.
fail_when: Two supertasks; supertask used as promo; two primaries; danger used without real consequences.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A second primary class that beats Actions one-primary.
